question: Should crawl-remote deployments permanently retain this hidden D1 canary and reject rollback to runtimes that do not declare canary support?
rationale: The choice intentionally narrows rollback compatibility and creates durable operational data, so correctness tests cannot substitute for maintainer acceptance of the release policy.

options.title: Approve permanent canary
options.body: Land the prerequisites first and accept the retained canary plus canary-aware rollback floor as the supported deployment contract.

options.title: Preserve legacy rollback
options.body: Rework the design around disposable or release-scoped canaries so older runtimes remain eligible rollback targets.

options.title: Pause this layer
options.body: Keep the draft unmerged until maintainers settle the long-term canary lifecycle and rollback policy.

recommendation.title: Approve permanent canary
recommendation.body: Land the prerequisites first and accept the retained canary plus canary-aware rollback floor as the supported deployment contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current Gitcrawl evidence and deployment stack and can present the intended operational contract for approval.
